LEONORINGCAST.name: Eleanor of England
LEONORINGCAST.summary: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Her life was connected with Castile, England.

KERANARM.name: Keran of Lampron
KERANARM.summary: Wife of Leo II and mother of a large royal lineage, she appears alongside her family in a famous Armenian manuscript image. Her sons occupied the crown or established links with Byzantium and Cyprus, giving this generation a great Mediterranean projection.

GASTON4FOIX.name: Gaston IV of Foix
GASTON4FOIX.summary: His marriage to Leonor of Navarre linked the house of Foix to the Navarre succession. He combined his Pyrenean interests with service to the French monarchy.

governmentNotes.Desde 1425 Bigorra la gobernaron los con: From 1425 Bigorre was ruled by the counts of Foix.

LEONORANJOU.name: Eleanor of Anjou
LEONORANJOU.summary: Her marriage to Frederick of Sicily sealed the rapprochement between the houses of Anjou and Barcelona after Caltabellotta. She was the mother of Peter II and the next generation of the island monarchy. The family bond did not prevent the two crowns from continuing to dispute rights and territories.

JUANAINGSIC.name: Joan of England
JUANAINGSIC.role: Queen consort of Sicily · Countess consort of Toulouse
JUANAINGSIC.summary: Daughter of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine, she married William II of Sicily in 1177. Widowed, she accompanied her brother Richard on the third crusade and in 1196 married Raymond VI of Toulouse. She died in 1199 and was buried in Fontevraud.

governmentNotes.Esposa de Guillermo II de Sicilia (1177): Wife of William II of Sicily (1177) and, after widowing and accompanying her brother Richard in the crusade, of Raymond VI of Toulouse (1196).

PETER2CYPRUS.name: Peter II of Cyprus
PETER2CYPRUS.summary: He inherited the crown as a minor after his father was murdered. The war with Genoa ended with the loss of Famagusta and heavy obligations for the monarchy. He died without surviving offspring, so his uncle Jacob succeeded him.

governmentNotes.Título dinástico sin dominio territorial: Dynastic title without territorial rule over Jerusalem.

JOANNAVBRET.name: Joan of Navarre, Duchess of Brittany
JOANNAVBRET.summary: Daughter of Charles II of Navarre, she married first John IV of Brittany and was the mother of several members of the next generation of dukes. She later married Henry IV of England.
JOANNAVBRET.biography: Daughter of Charles II of Navarre, she married first John IV of Brittany and was the mother of several members of the next generation of dukes. She later married Henry IV of England. Her career directly links Navarre, Britain and the English monarchy, and explains the kinship that runs through the political divisions of the time.

LUDOVICO2SAL.name: Ludovico II of Saluzzo
LUDOVICO2SAL.summary: He succeeded his father in Saluzzo and sought support in Milan, Monferrato and France. His military career led him to serve the French kings during the Italian Wars.
LUDOVICO2SAL.biography: He succeeded his father in Saluzzo and sought support in Milan, Monferrato and France. His military career led him to serve the French kings during the Italian Wars. The marriage to Margarita de Foix-Candale reinforced that orientation. At her death there was a child heir and a regency that prolonged the political influence of the Marquise.

governmentNotes.Ludovico II heredó de su padre. Su madre: Louis II inherited from his father. His mother Elizabeth of Montferrat connected him with the neighbouring marquis and with the House of Savoy.

ALEXIOS4TREB.name: Alejo IV of Trebizond
ALEXIOS4TREB.summary: He succeeded Manuel III and died during the rebellion of his son Juan. Sources disagree on his birth, which is shown as interval. Her marriage to Theodora links the imperial family to the Cantacucians.

governmentNotes.La edad descrita por Clavijo apunta haci: The age described by Clavijo points to 1379; another identification with Basil leads to 1382. The discrepancy is preserved.
governmentNotes.Alejo continuó la línea de Manuel. Se ma: Away he continued Manuel's line. The probable date of 1417 and the note on the uncertainty of death are kept.

JOANFITZDESMOND.name: Joan FitzGerald, condesa de Ormond
JOANFITZDESMOND.summary: Daughter of James of Desmond, she linked the Fitzgeralds to the Butlers by marriage to James of Ormond. After being widowed, she finally married Gerald of Desmond. Her family alliances crossed the political rivalry between the two houses.

BONIF3MON.name: Bonifacio III of Montferrat
BONIF3MON.summary: Son of John Jacobo, he succeeded his brother William VIII when expectations about the Monferrato inheritance already affected Savoy and Saluzzo. His sons William IX and John George extended the male line of the Paleologists.
BONIF3MON.biography: Son of John Jacobo, he succeeded his brother William VIII when expectations about the Monferrato inheritance already affected Savoy and Saluzzo. His sons William IX and John George extended the male line of the Paleologists. His government maintained a difficult relationship with Milan and also sought French protection.

governmentNotes.El marquesado pasó al hermano de Guiller: The marquess passed to William VIII's brother. William's daughters and his marriages maintained hereditary expectations, but they did not replace Bonifacio's access.

FERN2TIROL.name: Ferdinand II, Archduke of Austria
FERN2TIROL.summary: Archduch, son of Emperor Ferdinand I, governor of Bohemia and later lord of the Tyrol from 1564. Married to Philippine Welser, he assembled in the castle of Ambras one of the great collections of the Renaissance.

governmentNotes.Gobernó Tirol y los territorios anterior: He ruled Tyrol and the former Austrian territories by the partition of 1564.

MARIALUISAESP1745.name: Maria Luisa of Spain
MARIALUISAESP1745.summary: Consort of the Borbón dynasty. Her life was connected with Spain, Tuscany, Holy Roman Empire.

DAVIDTREB.name: David of Trebizond
DAVIDTREB.summary: Last emperor of Trebizond, he sought outside support before the Ottoman conquest of 1461. He was executed in 1463. The loss of the government and its death were separate events; the file preserves both dates.

governmentNotes.David sucedió a su hermano. La fecha de: David succeeded his brother. The date 1460 follows the revision of contemporary documentation against earlier dates.

BONALUX.name: Bona of Luxembourg
BONALUX.summary: Consort of the Luxemburgo dynasty. Their life was connected with France.

LEOP5TIROL.name: Leopold V of Austria-Tyrol
LEOP5TIROL.summary: Leopold V was governor of Tyrol on behalf of his brother Ferdinand II from 1619. The transfer of hereditary dominion was done in stages and culminated in 1630. He founded the new Thyros branch of the Habsburgs.

governmentNotes.Gobernador en nombre de su hermano Ferna: Governor in the name of his brother Ferdinand II; hereditary sovereignty was transferred to him in stages until 1630.
governmentNotes.Gobernante de Tirol y las tierras anteri: Governor of Tyrol and the former Austrian lands by cession of Ferdinand II.

AMALRICTYRE.name: Amalric of Lusignan, Lord of Tyre
AMALRICTYRE.summary: Brother of Henry II, he removed him from the government of Cyprus and exercised the administration of the island. His marriage to Elizabeth of Armenia connected the Lusignan with the Cilician succession. He was murdered, which allowed Henry to return.

JUANAHABS.name: Joanna of Austria, Grand Duchess of Tuscany
JUANAHABS.summary: Consort of the Habsburgo dynasty. Her life was connected with Tuscany.

MANUEL2PALA.name: Manuel II Palaiologos
MANUEL2PALA.summary: Byzantine emperor since 1391. He traveled through Western Europe seeking help against the Ottomans; Bayezid's defeat at Tamerlan in 1402 gave Constantinople a respite.

JOHN4BRET.name: John IV of Brittany
JOHN4BRET.summary: He inherited his father's cause, John de Montfort, and ended up imposing himself after the Battle of Auray. The agreement of Guérande consolidated his ducal position.
JOHN4BRET.biography: He inherited his father's cause, John de Montfort, and ended up imposing himself after the Battle of Auray. The agreement of Guérande consolidated his ducal position. His government was marked by relations with France and England; his marriage to Joan of Navarre added to the Breton house a connection with the Évreux.

JUAN2BRET.name: John II of Brittany
JUAN2BRET.summary: Son of John I and Blanche of Champagne, he married Beatrice of England. With him the Breton ducal heritage, the Navarre connection of his mother and the English of his wife converge. His son Arthur II was the father of the lines between which the duchy would later be contested.

FERN1TOSC.name: Ferdinando I de’ Medici
FERN1TOSC.summary: He left the cardinalate race to succeed his brother in Tuscany. He pushed the port of Livorno and sought to expand the diplomatic margins of the Medici.

JUANAEVREUX.name: Joan of Évreux
JUANAEVREUX.role: Queen consort of France and Navarre
JUANAEVREUX.summary: Daughter of Louis of Évreux and Margaret of Artois, she married Charles IV of France. Her marriage connected the branch of Évreux with the main line of the chief kings.
JUANAEVREUX.biography: Daughter of Louis of Évreux and Margaret of Artois, she married Charles IV of France. Her marriage connected the branch of Évreux with the main line of the chief kings. Crowned in 1326, she became a widow in 1328 and became pregnant; the birth of a daughter, Blanca, future duchess of Orleans, left the throne to Philip VI of Valois. She survived the monarch for decades and died in 1371.

governmentNotes.Reina consorte de Francia y de Navarra d: Queen consort of France and Navarre from her marriage to Charles IV in 1325 until the king's death in 1328; crowned in 1326. She did not exercise her own government.

ISABPORT3.name: Isabella of Portugal
ISABPORT3.summary: Daughter of the infant John of Portugal, she was the second wife of John II of Castile (1447) and mother of Isabel the Catholic and the infant Alfonso. Widowed since 1454, she lived in retirement in Arévalo until her death in 1496.

ALEXIOS2TREB.name: Alejo II of Trebizond
ALEXIOS2TREB.summary: He defended the autonomy of his empire against the tutelage of Andronicus II and negotiated the commercial access of Genoese and Venetians. His marriage to Djiadjak Jakeli strengthened the connection with Samtsje and the Georgian elites.

MICHELEANTONIOSAL.name: Miguel Antonio of Saluzzo
MICHELEANTONIOSAL.summary: The son of Ludovico II and Margarita of Foix-Candale, he inherited Saluzzo as a child. He developed his career in the service of the French monarchy, while his mother retained a decisive role in the marquessate.
MICHELEANTONIOSAL.biography: The son of Ludovico II and Margarita of Foix-Candale, he inherited Saluzzo as a child. He developed his career in the service of the French monarchy, while his mother retained a decisive role in the marquessate. His death without issue opened a dispute between his brothers, whose political positions were divided between France and the emperor.

governmentNotes.El heredero era todavía niño. Su madre M: The heir was still a child. His mother, Margarita de Foix-Candale, was the guardian and later held governmental functions during his son's absence.

GIORGI10KARTLI.name: George X of Kartli
GIORGI10KARTLI.summary: He took over the government after his father Simon was captured by the Ottomans. He cooperated with Abbas I against them and tried to open contacts with Russia. His descendants connect Kartli's succession to the court of Teimuraz I of Kakheti.

SANFRANBORJA.name: Francis Borgia
SANFRANBORJA.summary: He left court life and his ducal position to enter the Society of Jesus. He became Superior General of the order and was canonized later.

RICHARDETAMPES.name: Richard of Brittany
RICHARDETAMPES.summary: Son of John IV of Brittany and Joan of Navarre, he belonged to a smaller branch of the Montfort family. He married Margaret of Orleans, linking the Breton house with the Valois-Orleans.
RICHARDETAMPES.biography: Son of John IV of Brittany and Joan of Navarre, he belonged to a smaller branch of the Montfort family. He married Margaret of Orleans, linking the Breton house with the Valois-Orleans. He died before his son Francis II inherited the duchy; the importance of his line became visible in the next generation.

ANNACLEVESNEUBURG.name: Anne of Jülich-Cleves-Berg
ANNACLEVESNEUBURG.summary: Consort of the La Marck dynasty. Her life was connected with Jülich, Cleves, Berg.

ISABAUST.name: Isabella of Austria
ISABAUST.summary: Daughter of Philip the Beautiful and Joanna of Castile, she married Christian II of Denmark. Her marriage connected the Kalmar crisis to the Habsburg network. After Cristian's deposition she accompanied the family to exile in the Netherlands, where she died.

BEATSABPROV.name: Beatrice of Savoy
BEATSABPROV.summary: Daughter of Thomas I of Savoy, she married Ramon Berenguer IV of Provence. Her daughters were linked to the French and English monarchies and the houses of Anjou and Cornwall.
BEATSABPROV.biography: Daughter of Thomas I of Savoy, she married Ramon Berenguer IV of Provence. Her daughters were linked to the French and English monarchies and the houses of Anjou and Cornwall. This family allows to travel from the Alps several of the great political connections of the 13th century; it should not be confused with its niece Beatriz, linked to Saluzzo and Sicily.

FREDANSBACH.name: Frederick I of Brandenburg-Ansbach
FREDANSBACH.summary: Margrave of Ansbach, 1486–1515. Margrave of the Hohenzollern dynasty.

JUANLUDSAL.name: John Ludovico of Saluzzo
JUANLUDSAL.summary: Son of Ludwig II and Margaret of Foix-Candale, he defended a favourable orientation towards Charles V. His mother and brothers removed him from power on several occasions.
JUANLUDSAL.biography: Son of Ludwig II and Margaret of Foix-Candale, he defended a favourable orientation towards Charles V. His mother and brothers removed him from power on several occasions. He again claimed the marquessate upon the death of Gabriel, but France did not recognize his rights. His card distinguishes the family claim from a lasting territorial domain.

COSIMO3TOSC.name: Cosimo III of Tuscany
COSIMO3TOSC.summary: Grand Duke of Tuscany between 1670 and 1723, the longest reign of the dynasty. His government coincided with the state's economic stagnation and the succession crisis of the Medici.

INGEBORGVALDEMAR.name: Ingeborg Valdemarsdatter
INGEBORGVALDEMAR.summary: Daughter of Valdemar IV and sister of Margaret. Her marriage to Henry of Mecklemburg linked the Danish house with a family that also claimed rights in Sweden. Through her daughter Maria was the grandmother of Eric of Pomerania: this is the family connection that made her promotion by Margarita possible.

SOLOMON2IMER.name: Solomon II of Imereti
SOLOMON2IMER.summary: He came to power with the support of his grandfather Heraclius II and challenged the crown to David II. Russian expansion ended with its deposition in 1810. He died in exile in Trebizond, after trying to reclaim the kingdom.

MARGPALEO.name: Margaret Palaiologina
MARGPALEO.summary: Daughter of William IX and Anne of Alençon, her marriage to Frederick II Gonzaga was decisive for the transmission of Monferrato to that house. The inheritance required an imperial resolution and was not an automatic effect of the wedding.
MARGPALEO.biography: Daughter of William IX and Anne of Alençon, her marriage to Frederick II Gonzaga was decisive for the transmission of Monferrato to that house. The inheritance required an imperial resolution and was not an automatic effect of the wedding. After being widowed she exercised the regency of her sons and maintained an intense diplomatic activity between Mantua, Casale and the great European courts.

ALEXANDRULAPU.name: Alexander Lăpușneanu
ALEXANDRULAPU.summary: He ruled Moldova in two stages, separated by a deposition. His marriage to Ruxandra Rareș strengthened ties with Petru Rareș's offspring.
ALEXANDRULAPU.biography: He ruled Moldova in two stages, separated by a deposition. His marriage to Ruxandra Rareș strengthened ties with Petru Rareș's offspring. His son Bogdan inherited as a minor. The violence attributed to the prince also inspired later literature, which must be distinguished from the documentation of his government.

JUAN2BRAB.name: John II of Brabant
JUAN2BRAB.summary: It happened to John I in Brabant and Limburg. He married Margaret of England and was the father of John III. The marriage maintained the English connection of the duchy, while the two ducal dignities continued to be transmitted under one house.

governmentNotes.Juan II heredó los ducados de su padre,: John II inherited his father's duchies, dying after a tournament. Brabante and Limburg shared the title without losing his identities.

LEOPOLD1ANHALT.name: Leopold I, Prince of Anhalt-Dessau
LEOPOLD1ANHALT.summary: Ascanian prince of Anhalt-Dessau from 1693 to 1747. During his minority rule his mother, Enriqueta Catalina. Known as the Old Dessauer for his military career in the service of Prussia, he maintained his own principality.

governmentNotes.Sucede a su padre siendo menor, bajo la: He succeeded his father as a minor, under the tutelage and regency of his mother until 1698. His Prussian military service does not incorporate the principality into Prussia.

DAREJANIMER.name: Darejan of Kakheti
DAREJANIMER.summary: Daughter of Teimuraz I, she was consort queen of Imericia and a decisive figure in her succession disputes. After the death of Alexander III she intervened against Bagrat V and promoted Vajtang Tchutchunashvili. She died during another Western court crisis.

ROGER4FOIX.name: Roger IV of Foix
ROGER4FOIX.summary: Count of Foix in the 13th century, he preceded the generation that linked the county with Bearne in a lasting way. His son Roger Bernard III entered into the marriage that sustained this hereditary union.
ROGER4FOIX.biography: Count of Foix in the 13th century, he preceded the generation that linked the county with Bearne in a lasting way. His son Roger Bernard III entered into the marriage that sustained this hereditary union. His daughter Esclaramunda married James II of Mallorca, opening another connection between the Pyrenees and the Mediterranean.

CLEMHUNGRIA.name: Clementia of Hungary
CLEMHUNGRIA.summary: Consort of the Anjou-Hungría dynasty. Their life was connected with France.

DAVIDDATUNA.name: David Datuna of Kakheti
DAVIDDATUNA.summary: Son of Teimuraz I and Jorashan, he fought in the battle against Rostom and died at the Battle of Magharo. His son Heraclius continued the royal line of the Kajetia, from which Teimuraz II and Heraclius II would proceed.

TEOB3CHAMP.name: Theobald III of Champagne
TEOB3CHAMP.summary: Count of Champagne and husband of Blanche of Navarre, died before the birth of his son Teobaldo. The widow had to defend the condal inheritance during the minority of the child. Although Theobald III did not reign in Navarre, his marriage prepared the bond by which his offspring reached that crown.

WEN2.name: Wenceslaus II of Bohemia
WEN2.summary: He gathered the crowns of Bohemia and Poland and turned the silver wealth of Kutná Hora into a support of his power. His dynastic expansion prepared his son's candidacy for the Hungarian throne.

PHILIPLOUISNEUBURG.name: Philip Louis of the Palatinate-Neuburg
PHILIPLOUISNEUBURG.summary: He ruled the Duchy of Pfalz-Neuburg from 1569. He was not elector of the Palatinate: his marriage to Anne of Jülich-Cleves-Berg prepared the subsequent renal claim of his son.

TAMARIMERKART.name: Tamar of Imereti, Queen of Kartli
TAMARIMERKART.summary: Daughter of Bagrat III of Imericia, her marriage to Luarsab I united the two western and eastern branches of the Bagrationi. She was the mother of Simon I and David XI, rivals who followed different policies against the Safavid power.

FERNKARLTIROL.name: Ferdinand Charles of Austria-Tyrol
FERNKARLTIROL.summary: Fernando Carlos inherited Tirol in 1632 as a child. His mother Claudia de Medici ruled as regent until 1646; then she exercised power personally until her death in 1662.

governmentNotes.Titular desde 1632; gobernó bajo la rege: Titled from 1632; he ruled under his mother's regency until 1646 and then by himself.

MARGBAV.name: Margaret of Bavaria-Straubing
MARGBAV.summary: Consort of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Her life was connected with Borgoña, Bavaria.

CARLOSEMANUELCAR.name: Charles Emmanuel of Savoy-Carignano
CARLOSEMANUELCAR.summary: Prince of Carignano of the Saboya-Carignano dynasty. Their life was connected with Saboya, Piedmont.

SANCHAMALL.name: Sancha of Majorca
SANCHAMALL.summary: Consort of the Barcelona dynasty. Their life was connected with Naples.

CARLOTASAB.name: Charlotte of Savoy
CARLOTASAB.summary: Consort of the Saboya dynasty. Her life was connected with France, Saboya.

JACOBO5ESCOCIA.name: James V of Scotland
JACOBO5ESCOCIA.summary: He sought to assert his authority over the nobility and upheld the French alliance. His death left the crown to Maria Stuart when he was only a few days old.

JELENAZRIN.name: Jelena Zrinski
JELENAZRIN.summary: Daughter of Petar Zrinski and Anne Katarina Frankopan, she married Francis I Rákóczi and was the mother of Francis II. She defended Munkács against imperial forces.
JELENAZRIN.biography: Daughter of Petar Zrinski and Anne Katarina Frankopan, she married Francis I Rákóczi and was the mother of Francis II. She defended Munkács against imperial forces. After her second marriage to Imre Thököly she shared the Ottoman exile. Her life links Croatian heritage with the wars of Hungary and Transylvania.

JOHANNAELISAHOLST.name: Joanna Elisabeth of Holstein-Gottorp
JOHANNAELISAHOLST.summary: Regent of Anhalt-Zerbst, 1747–1752 (regency). Princess of the Holstein-Gottorp dynasty.

governmentNotes.Regencia durante la minoría de Federico: Regency during the minority of Frederick Augustus; it does not continue until the end of her life.

SOPHIADOROTHEAHAN.name: Sophia Dorothea of Hanover
SOPHIADOROTHEAHAN.summary: Consort of the Hannover dynasty. Her life was connected with Hannover, Prussia.

JELENASUBICBOS.name: Jelena Šubić
JELENASUBICBOS.summary: A member of the Šubić of Bribir, she married Vladislav of Bosnia and was the mother of Tvrtko I. Her intervention during the youth of the future king places this Croatian noblewoman at the center of Bosnian continuity. The family connection did not make the Kotromanić into a male branch of the Šubić.

MARIATUDOR.name: Mary Tudor
MARIATUDOR.summary: Consort of the Tudor dynasty. Her life was connected with France, England.

JUANAVALNAV.name: Joan of Valois
JUANAVALNAV.summary: Consort of the Valois dynasty. Her life was connected with Navarre, France.

ROGERBERNARDO2FOIX.name: Roger Bernard II of Foix
ROGERBERNARDO2FOIX.summary: Son and successor of Raymond Roger, he was Count of Foix from 1223 to 1241. His marriage to Ermesenda (1208) united the Viscounty of Castellbó and Cerdaña to the house. His protection from the Albigensians and his rejection of the Inquisition earned him further excommunications.

LUISVICTORCAR.name: Louis Victor of Savoy-Carignano
LUISVICTORCAR.summary: Prince of Carignano of the Saboya-Carignano dynasty. Their life was connected with Saboya, Piedmont.

VICTORAMADEO1CAR.name: Victor Amadeus I of Savoy-Carignano
VICTORAMADEO1CAR.summary: Prince of Carignano of the Saboya-Carignano dynasty. Their life was connected with Saboya, Piedmont.

JUANAVALOIS.name: Joan of Valois
JUANAVALOIS.summary: Consort of the Valois dynasty. Her life was connected with Hainaut, Holland.

MARGORLEANSBRET.name: Margaret of Orléans
MARGORLEANSBRET.summary: Daughter of Louis of Orleans and Valentina Visconti, she married Richard of Brittany. Her son Francis II became ruler of the duchy and father of Anne of Brittany. Through Margarita, that Breton heiress was connected to the families of Orleans and Milan before her own royal marriages.

MIGPAZ.name: Miguel da Paz
MIGPAZ.summary: Prince of the Avís dynasty. Their life was connected with Portugal, Castile, Aragon.

ASCANIOCOLONNA.name: Ascanio Colonna
ASCANIOCOLONNA.summary: Duke of the Colonna dynasty. His life was connected with Naples, Papal States.

WILHELMINEAMALIA.name: Wilhelmine Amalia of Brunswick-Lüneburg
WILHELMINEAMALIA.summary: Consort of the Welf dynasty. Their life was connected with Holy Roman Empire.

BLANCANJ.name: Blanche of Anjou
BLANCANJ.summary: Consort of the Anjou dynasty. Her life was connected with Aragon.

LEO5CILICIA.name: Leo V of Cilician Armenia
LEO5CILICIA.summary: Last effective king of Cilician Armenia, he lost Sis to the Mamluks in 1375 and spent years in captivity. Released, he traveled through European courts seeking support. His stay in Castile and his death in Paris connect the end of the kingdom with Western Europe.

JUANABR.name: Joanna of Brabant
JUANABR.summary: Duchess of Brabant, 1355 to 1406. Duchess of the Brabant dynasty.

governmentNotes.Juana, la hija mayor superviviente de Ju: Joan, the eldest surviving daughter of John III, inherited the duchy. Her right did not prevent the opposition of Louis de Male, husband of her sister Margarita.

STEPHENTHOMASBOS.name: Stephen Thomas of Bosnia
STEPHENTHOMASBOS.summary: King of Bosnia in the decades before the Ottoman conquest. His reign was marked by internal religious tensions and increasing pressure from Hungary and Mehmed II.

MARIACAST.name: Maria of Castile
MARIACAST.summary: Consort of the Trastámara dynasty. Her life was connected with Aragon.

DJURADJBRANKOVIC.name: Đurađ Branković
DJURADJBRANKOVIC.summary: He succeeded his uncle Stefan Lazarević and organized his power center in Smederevo. The Ottoman conquest interrupted his rule between 1439 and 1444.
DJURADJBRANKOVIC.biography: He succeeded his uncle Stefan Lazarević and organized his power center in Smederevo. The Ottoman conquest interrupted his rule between 1439 and 1444. His restoration depended on the balance between Hungary and the Ottoman Porte. The children and grandchildren of his marriage to Irene Cantacuzena prolonged the history of the Branković beyond the loss of territory.

governmentNotes.Desplazado por la conquista otomana; res: Displaced by the Ottoman conquest; restored in 1444.

CHRISTIANALBERTHG.name: Christian Albert de Holstein-Gottorp
CHRISTIANALBERTHG.summary: Duke of Holstein, 1659–1695 (branch). Duke of the Holstein-Gottorp dynasty.

ANNASAVOYBYZ.name: Anne of Savoy
ANNASAVOYBYZ.summary: Daughter of Amadeus V of Savoy and wife of Andronikos III Palaiologos. She was regent for her son John V during the civil war against John Cantacuceno (1341–1347).

ALFONSOFADRIQUE.name: Alfonso Fadrique
ALFONSOFADRIQUE.role: Vicar-general of Athens · Count of Salona
ALFONSOFADRIQUE.summary: The natural son of Frederick II of Sicily, he ruled from 1317 the Catalan duchies as vicar general of his half-brother William. He conquered Siderocastro and southern Thessaly, with whom he formed the duchy of Neopatria in 1319. He married Marulla of Verona in 1317 and founded the branch of the Fadrique, counts of Salona and lords of Aegina.

governmentNotes.Hijo natural del rey de Sicilia, gobernó: Natural son of the king of Sicily, he ruled the duchy in the name of his half-brother William.
governmentNotes.Conquistó Siderocastro y la Tesalia meri: He conquered Siderecastro and southern Thessaly and formed the duchy in 1319.
governmentNotes.Parece que obtuvo Salona después de la c: It seems that he obtained Salona after the Catalan conquest of 1311; with it he became a county. The year of acquisition is approximate.

DJORDJEMAKSIM.name: Đorđe Branković, Maksim
DJORDJEMAKSIM.summary: Son of Stefan and Angelina, he retained the title of Serbian despot in exile. He abandoned secular life and took the name Maximus. His religious activity and his relationship with Krušedol continued the family's presence in the region. It should not be confused with the eponymous 17th-century historian.

governmentNotes.Dignidad conservada en los dominios húng: Dignity retained in the Hungarian dominions, without effective government of Serbia.

GIORGI12GEO.name: George XII of Kartli-Kakheti
GIORGI12GEO.summary: Last king of Kartli-Kajetia, he inherited a monarchy weakened by the Persian invasion and family disputes. He requested Russian protection, but his death preceded the annexation of the kingdom. Dynastic succession did not become another effective reign.

LOUISEHENRIETTEORANGE.name: Louise Henriette of Orange-Nassau
LOUISEHENRIETTEORANGE.summary: Consort of the Nassau dynasty. Their life was connected with Low Countries, Brandenburg.

JUAN1MARCH.name: John I de Borbón-La Marche
JUAN1MARCH.summary: Count of La Marche, 1362–1393. Count of the Bourbon dynasty.

FRED3HOLGOTT.name: Frederick III de Holstein-Gottorp
FRED3HOLGOTT.summary: Duke of Holstein, 1616–1659 (branch). Duke of the Holstein-Gottorp dynasty.

BAYEZID2OSM.name: Bayezid II
BAYEZID2OSM.summary: Ottoman Sultan who ruled between the great conquests of Mehmed II and the expansion of Selim I. His reign consolidated institutions and territories as the dynasty extended its influence over the Mediterranean and the Balkans.

SELIM1OSM.name: Selim I
